title: Support Micro-ops Compiler and Safe Execution Runtime
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Create a compiler and light-weight runtime that converts ad-hoc admin scripts and runbook steps into verifiable, sandboxed 'micro-ops' (tasklets) that can be scheduled, simulated, and executed with RBAC and audit guarantees.

Motivation: Oncall engineers frequently run bespoke shell snippets or ad-hoc admin scripts during incidents. These are error-prone, hard to rehearse, and have inconsistent telemetry/audit trails. We want a developer-friendly path to turn those snippets into reusable, safe tasklets that integrate with runbooks-as-tasks and the support automation surface (playflows, quick fixes, and simulated rehearsals).

Scope: This ticket covers the prototype compiler + runtime and integration points: (1) a small DSL/annotation pattern for existing scripts (bash/python) and a transform that emits a typed micro-op package, (2) a sandboxed runtime with permission scoping and dry-run semantics, (3) a simulator that can replay a runbook composed of micro-ops against synthetic cluster state, and (4) telemetry/audit hooks that record intent, parameters, pre/post checks, and rollbacks.

Out of scope: full migration of existing playbook corpus (will be separate migration effort), UI polish in Console (prototype CLI & API only).
acceptance_criteria: A CLI tool that compiles an annotated admin script into a micro-op bundle with metadata (inputs, outputs, safety-checks) and a machine-readable manifest.
A runtime that executes micro-op bundles under a confined user profile; supports dry-run mode that validates preconditions and outputs simulated trace without mutating resources.
Simulator can run a 3-step runbook composed of compiled micro-ops and produce a deterministic trace file used for rehearsals.
Audit events emitted to existing telemetry pipeline with operation id, actor, bundle version, parameters, and result summary.
Basic RBAC enforcement: only identities in operator-admin or operator-runner can execute mutation modes; others limited to dry-run or review-only.
A design doc and a reference PR (prototype) linked in artifacts and reviewed by security and oncall leads.
steps: Design doc + interface sketch (inputs, manifests, telemetry schema) — 2d
Prototype DSL/annotation and compiler that extracts typed params and safety-checks — 4d
Implement minimal sandbox runtime (process isolation, syscall whitelist, env scrub) + dry-run logic — 5d
Build simulator harness that can feed synthetic state and assert expected traces — 3d
Hook telemetry (audit events) and add initial RBAC enforcement through token exchange — 2d
Ship prototype PR, gather feedback from oncall rotation, and iterate — 3d
comments: 2025-03-10 Aisha Kapoor: Created ticket. Initial idea based on recurring incident post-mortem where ad-hoc s3-rollbacks diverged across runbooks.

2025-03-12 Ben Cho: Spike finished — evaluated two approaches: compile-to-WASM vs interpreter with strict linters. Chose interpreter+bytecode for faster iteration; WASM reserved if we need cross-language sandboxing.
2025-03-14 Miguel Santos (security): Reviewed sandbox model; requested syscall whitelist, KMS usage for secrets, and clear deny-by-default network policy. Marked security_review_required=true.
2025-03-16 Sarah Lin (oncall): Ran the simulator against the nightly synthetic cluster. Found missing precondition check for DB migration step; added 'can-read-schema' precheck to manifest schema.
2025-03-18 Ben Cho: Opened prototype PR and demoed CLI to SRE guild. Feedback: add better error messages for parameter validation and make telemetry event ids deterministic for replay correlation.
2025-03-20 Aisha Kapoor: Updated acceptance criteria to require deterministic trace output for simulator; set due_date to 2025-04-01.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Execing arbitrary scripts increases blast radius. Mitigation: compile step enforces annotations and explicit opt-in for mutation; runtime enforces syscall and network policies plus RBAC token exchange.
Risk: Divergence between compiled micro-ops and original behavior. Mitigation: require a one-time validation run against a staging cluster and require author sign-off in PR for migration.
Risk: Telemetry sprawl. Mitigation: reuse existing audit schema and push only condensed event summaries; heavy payloads go to gs:// traces for offline analysis.
